title: Robotics Software Engineer
tagline: Make machines perceive, plan and move in the real world.
about: Robotics software engineers write the code that lets robots sense their surroundings, decide what to do and act safely: perception, localisation, planning and control. The field blends programming, maths, physics and machine learning.
Simulation lets you learn most of it without buying hardware, and ROS 2 is the industry's common toolkit.
day: Develop perception from cameras and lidar

phases.title: Programming foundations
phases.goal: Write small programs confidently and use the tools every developer uses daily.

nodes.d: Pick Python and get fluent with the basics before anything else. Fluency in one language transfers to every other.
links: CS50x: Harvard's intro to computer science

nodes.d: Developers live in the command line: navigating files, running programs and chaining tools together.
links: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)
OverTheWire: Bandit (learn the shell by playing)

nodes.d: Version control is non-negotiable: every job uses it. Commit early, branch for experiments, open pull requests.
Break problems down, read errors calmly, use a debugger and print statements deliberately.
links: Exercism: practice in 70+ languages with mentoring

phases.title: Maths & physics for robots
phases.goal: The language robots are described in.

nodes.d: Rotations, homogeneous transforms and coordinate frames.
Robots are never certain where they are.
links: Seeing Theory: visual probability and statistics

nodes.d: How joints and wheels map to motion.
Make systems follow a target smoothly.
Nodes, topics, services, actions and launch files.
Test robots safely in Gazebo before touching hardware.
Detect and track objects with cameras.
links: Stanford CS231n: deep learning for vision

project.d: A ROS 2 robot in Gazebo that maps a room, localises itself and drives to goals while avoiding obstacles.

nodes.d: Estimate position and build maps at the same time.
Find safe, efficient paths for robots and arms.
links: Red Blob Games: interactive game-dev algorithms

nodes.d: Learn behaviours from data and simulation.
Robots move in the physical world; failures matter.

project.d: A complete autonomy demo (simulated arm picking objects using vision, or a mobile robot navigating a building) with a video and technical write-up.

interview: Implement a filter or planner (for example A*).
Explain a robotics project in depth, including what failed.
